project.name: ai-trip
project.description: AI-powered travel itinerary planner that generates JSON-driven, editable itineraries with every location validated against Google Places. Supports collaborative trip planning, expense tracking, visa requirements, packing checklists, and reservation management.

nodes.name: Trip Planning & Itinerary
nodes.summary: Core business domain for creating, editing, and managing travel itineraries. Manages trips, day-by-day plans, activities, accommodations, travel segments, and ideas buckets. The structured JSON itinerary is the heart of the product.

businessRules: Every activity must have a Google Places-validated location (or null if enrichment failed)
Itinerary is JSON-driven and editable, never free-form chat
Trip access is role-based (owner, editor, viewer)
Drag-and-drop reordering triggers automatic travel segment recomputation
Activities can be promoted from the ideas bucket into the itinerary
crossDomainInteractions: Uses AI Generation domain to produce activity suggestions
Uses Places & Maps domain to enrich activity locations
Emits Activity Log events for Collaboration domain audit trail
Cost data flows into Expenses & Budget domain

nodes.name: AI Generation & Enrichment
nodes.summary: Handles intent-based AI itinerary generation using Google Gemini via the Vercel AI SDK. Translates natural-language prompts into structured itinerary actions (add, remove, optimize, reschedule, fill gaps, accommodation) and pairs every AI suggestion with Google Places verification.

businessRules: AI must never invent places — every suggestion is validated against Google Places
AI usage is rate-limited and metered per user
Intent-based pipeline: add | remove | modify | optimize | reschedule | fill_gaps | accommodation
Discuss agent powers conversational refinement separately from itinerary edits
Prompts must be sanitized to prevent injection
crossDomainInteractions: Produces activity drafts for the Trip Planning domain
Calls Places & Maps domain to resolve and enrich place names
Generates proposals and reviews that mutate trip state

nodes.name: Places & Maps Integration
nodes.summary: Wraps Google Maps Platform APIs (Places, Distance Matrix, Geocoding) to provide place search, place details, photo proxying, and travel-time computation. Every activity location in the system is grounded here.

businessRules: All AI-suggested places must be resolved to a Google place_id before persisting
Photo URLs are proxied through the backend (never expose API key to client)
Travel segments are recomputed when activities change order, time, or transport mode
Enrichment has a 1-hour cooldown per activity
crossDomainInteractions: Consumed by Trip Planning to anchor activities to real locations
Consumed by AI Generation to validate every candidate place
Powers cost derivation via place price_level for Expenses & Budget

nodes.name: Collaboration & Sharing
nodes.summary: Multi-user collaboration for trips including member roles, invite tokens, public share links, activity comments, voting, participant tracking, and audit logging. Enables teams to co-plan a trip.

businessRules: Roles are owner | editor | viewer with hierarchical permissions
Invite tokens are hashed before storage; raw token only sent in email
Public share links are read-only and revocable
Every mutating action is appended to the activity log audit trail
Each member may cast one up/down vote per activity
crossDomainInteractions: Gates all Trip Planning operations via requireTripAccess
Sends emails via the User & Auth domain's mail service for invites

nodes.name: User & Authentication
nodes.summary: User identity, authentication via BetterAuth, profile management, and user-scoped data such as passports, visited countries, and travel preferences. Provides the requireAuth middleware used across the API.

businessRules: Sensitive fields (passport numbers) are encrypted at rest
Passport expiry triggers proactive email notification
Auth required on every API route except public shared/auth endpoints
Passport nationality drives visa requirement lookups
crossDomainInteractions: Provides session.user.id to every other domain
Passport data feeds the Visa & Travel Documents domain
Profile preferences influence AI Generation prompts

nodes.name: Expenses & Budget
nodes.summary: Tracks per-trip expenses, currency conversion, exchange rate lookups, and cost estimates. Includes refresh-from-Google to auto-fill activity costs from place price_level data.

businessRules: Expenses are stored in their original currency with conversion at display time
Trip-wide currency conversion applies a single FX rate snapshot
Cost estimates can be derived from Google Places price_level
Refresh-from-Google updates stale cost estimates from current place data
crossDomainInteractions: Reads activity place data from Places & Maps for cost derivation
Linked to activities and reservations in Trip Planning

nodes.name: Travel Documents & Visa
nodes.summary: Manages flights, reservations, packing checklists, trip documents, and visa requirement checks. Includes scheduled cron tasks for passport expiry alerts and visa data import.

businessRules: Flight data is auto-refreshed from external API every 2 hours while trip is active
Visa requirements are checked against user's passport nationality
Packing templates can be global or user-owned
Cron-secured endpoints require Bearer token matching CRON_SECRET
Passport expiry job notifies users with travel within validity-risk window
crossDomainInteractions: Reads passport data from User & Auth for visa checks
Attaches flights and reservations to trips in Trip Planning
Layover tips use AI Generation for personalized suggestions

edges.description: AI generates structured activity drafts that are persisted into the itinerary
Every AI-suggested place is resolved and enriched via Google Maps before persistence
Activities reference Google place_ids; segments use Distance Matrix for travel times
Trip-scoped access control, comments, votes, and audit logs gate every mutation
Member identity, invite emails, and role checks resolve through the auth domain
Activity costs and reservations feed into trip expense totals
Cost estimates can be derived from Google Places price_level
Visa checks read the user's passport and nationality
Flights and reservations attach to trips; layovers tie into the itinerary
Layover-tips endpoint uses Gemini for personalized airport recommendations
